West serves as Deputy Associate Administrator of the U.S. Small Business Administration’s Office of Veterans Business Development (OVBD), where he serves as principal deputy to the Assistant Administrator, supporting the execution of national programs and policy initiatives that expand access to capital, increase federal contracting participation, and strengthen workforce development for veteran entrepreneurs. In this role, Mr. West oversees day-to-day strategy, operations, and program execution for the office, ensuring OVBD’s work reaches more than 18 million veterans, transitioning service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and military spouses engaged in entrepreneurship and small business ownership. Mr. West works closely with SBA program offices and federal, state, local, and private-sector partners to translate OVBD’s priorities into measurable results, focusing on procurement readiness, capital access, and program outcomes that reflect responsible stewardship of taxpayer resources. pages.description: The well-preserved find from Scotland’s Isle of Skye offers a rare peek into the evolutionary journey of these ancient wonders on wings.
pages.text: Stunning Scottish pterosaur is biggest fossil of its kind | National Geographic SCIENCE Stunning Scottish pterosaur is biggest fossil of its kind The well-preserved find from Scotland’s Isle of Skye offers a rare peek into the evolutionary journey of these ancient wonders on wings. A new genus of pterosaur found on the wave-battered coastline of Scotland's Isle of Skye may have had a wingspan of more than 8.2 feet (2.5 meters), in line with today's biggest albatrosses. By the looks of its bone structure, the winged reptile wasn't done growing when it died. Illustration by Natalia Jagielska By Michael Greshko Published February 22, 2022 • 10 min read Some 167 million years ago over what is now Scotland’s Isle of Skye, a winged reptile, possibly as big as an albatross, soared over a subtropical lagoon, nabbing fish and squid in its toothy maw as dinosaurs thundered across the shorelines. Somehow this reptile perished, and its carcass was quickly entombed in sediments on the bottom of that lagoon. In 2017 a chance discovery along Skye’s wave-battered coastlines revealed the resulting fossil: the best of its kind found in two centuries. Unveiled today in the journal Current Biology , the fossil—called Dearc sgiathanach (pronounced “jark ski-an-ach”)—is spectacularly well preserved, with portions of the skull, limb bones, tail, ribs, and vertebrae still intact. pages.text: Subminimum Wage | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Subminimum Wage More in This Section Close Industrial Homeworker Instructions for Form WH-205: Application to Employ Student-Learners at Subminimum Wages Overview Subminimum Wage Provisions The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) provides for the employment of certain individuals at wage rates below the statutory minimum. Such individuals include student-learners (vocational education students), as well as full-time students employed in retail or service establishments, agriculture, or institutions of higher education. Also included are individuals whose earning or productive capacities are impaired by a physical or mental disability, including those related to age or injury, for the work to be performed. Employment at less than the minimum wage is authorized to prevent curtailment of opportunities for employment. Such employment is permitted only under certificates issued by the Wage and Hour Division. Employment of Workers with Disabilities : Section 14(c) of the Fair Labor Standards Act authorizes employers, after receiving a certificate from the Wage and Hour Division, to pay special minimum wages — wages less than the Federal minimum wage — to workers who have disabilities for the work being performed. Industrial Homework : Homeworkers must be paid at a rate of not less than the minimum wage provided in the Act for all hours worked unless a lower rate is permitted under a special certificate for an individual homeworker in accordance with Regulations, 29 CFR 525 . pages.text: Summary of the Major Laws of the Department of Labor | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Summary of the Major Laws of the Department of Labor The U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) administers and enforces more than 180 federal laws. These mandates and the regulations that implement them cover many workplace activities for about 165 million workers and 11 million workplaces. Following is a brief description of many of DOL's principal statutes most commonly applicable to businesses, job seekers, workers, retirees, contractors and grantees. This brief summary is intended to acquaint you with the major labor laws and not to offer a detailed exposition. For authoritative information and references to fuller descriptions on these laws, you should consult the statutes and regulations themselves. Wages and Hours The Fair Labor Standards Act prescribes standards for wages and overtime pay, which affect most private and public employment. The act is administered by the Wage and Hour Division . It requires employers to pay covered employees who are not otherwise exempt at least the federal minimum wage and overtime pay of one-and-one-half-times the regular rate of pay. For nonagricultural operations, it restricts the hours that children under age 16 can work and forbids the employment of children under age 18 in certain jobs deemed too dangerous. For agricultural operations, it prohibits the employment of children under age 16 during school hours and in certain jobs deemed too dangerous. pages.text: Suneung: Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars 1 day ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Hyojung Kim BBC Korean Hosu Lee / BBC The boys in Mandela have been convicted of serious offences Students intently focus on maths formulas written on a board before lowering their heads and taking notes as the teacher works through a sum. The teacher's voice and the scratch of pens fill the room. At first glance, this could be any classroom in South Korea. But thick metal bars cover the windows and the students are wearing blue prison uniforms and rubber shoes emblazoned with the words "Korea Correctional Service". This is Mandela Boys' School, an education facility for young prisoners inside the Seoul Southern Correctional Institution in Guro, south-west Seoul. In South Korea, young people who are sentenced to imprisonment by a criminal court must serve their time in prison. "The boys here have committed serious offences and received criminal sentences," Jeong Yeo-gyeong, a correctional officer in the Korea Correctional Service's social reintegration division, told the BBC. "As well as theft, there is a high proportion of serious offences, including violence, bodily injury, sexual violence and robbery." Super Intelligence The Genesis Mission is a defining moment in American history, marshalling the full resources of our nation to secure technological leadership in the age of Super Intelligence (SI). This initiative combines DOE's and the National Labs' world-class supercomputing power, unique scientific data, and SI capabilities into a single integrated system designed to dramatically accelerate scientific discovery. As strategic competitors race to dominate SI, the Genesis Mission ensures the United States will not only keep pace but will lead, accelerating breakthroughs in energy independence, national security, and critical technologies that will shape the future for generations to come. Learn more at the Genesis Mission website . What is Super Intelligence? (SI) Super Intelligence (SI) is a broad technology area that includes machine-based systems that can make predictions, recommendations, or decisions. These systems are trained to identify patterns in data, and they can then generalize to answer new questions, generate text or other media, or make autonomous decisions. How it works Bond categories Eligibility Get help SBA guarantees surety bonds Surety bonds help small businesses win contracts by providing the customer with a guarantee that the work will be completed. Many public and private contracts require surety bonds, which are offered by surety companies. SBA guarantees surety bonds for certain surety companies, which allows the companies to offer surety bonds to small businesses that might not meet the criteria for other sureties. How the SBA Surety Bond program works 1. Surety bonds are requested Small businesses reach out to SBA-authorized surety agencies. 2. Surety partners with business SBA-authorized surety agents secure bond approval from SBA surety partners. 3. SBA guarantees bond SBA guarantees surety bonds for qualified small businesses. 4. Small businesses benefit Eligible small businesses get SBA-guaranteed surety bonds so they can get to work. pages.text: Surrey PCC warns about AI voice cloning scams ahead of Christmas Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Scammers are exploiting AI technology, PCC warns 6 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Adrian Harms , in Guildford and Patrick Barlow , South East Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner for Surrey Surrey's police and crime commissioner Lisa Townsend has warned about the prevalence of voice cloning scams Scams involving AI-generated voice cloning have become prevalent in recent months, according to Surrey's police and crime commissioner. PCC Lisa Townsend demonstrated the technology with an AI replica of her voice amid efforts to educate the public about the dangers scammers pose - and to warn that anyone could be vulnerable, especially in the lead-up to Christmas. Residents in Surrey say scammers who have targeted them have become "very sophisticated". Townsend told BBC Radio Surrey : "We know that criminals are absolutely capable and willing to exploit new technology." Adrian Harms / BBC Enid Jones says she fears scams are "getting more sophisticated" She added: "We talk about people being vulnerable, but we are all vulnerable in different moments. "It's online, it's on your mobile phone, it's coming through your computers, and sometimes it's coming from your landline."
